voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: Twenty twenty-four. The wood of an Easter Island tablet kept in Rome was dated. The tree was cut down around fifteen hundred.
Two centuries before Europeans arrived. If the writing is that old, islanders may have invented it alone. Only a handful of places ever have.
But dating the wood is not dating the carving. The authors say so themselves.
And this wood never grew on the island. It may have drifted ashore, or come off a European ship.
Fewer than thirty carved objects survive. The script has never been deciphered.
